# Scaffold generator: opt-in write gating and an explicit game-path migration flag

## Goal

As the engine maintainer, I want `game-repo-scaffold.ts` to stop overwriting
consumer-owned wiring by default and to stop applying the
`example-games/<game>/` → `src/` codemod to every file on every run, so a
re-scaffold of the live `tce-main-street` checkout can no longer silently gut
its build/test wiring.

Created from `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB` (producer decision Q2=A). That item's
acceptance criteria are carried over here in full; the `MS` item is closed once
this item exists.

## Producer decisions (2026-10-31)

- **Q1 = B — explicit selection, not a changed default.** Keep today's
  behaviour for fresh/extracted game repos; add `--only <file,...>`, `--force`
  and `--dry-run`; the main-street `scaffold` script opts in to `main.ts` only.
- **Q2 = A — this item owns the generator change**, test-first in the engine
  repo, followed by an engine pin bump in `tce-main-street`.
- **Q3 = A — `rewriteGameTreePaths` becomes opt-in** via
  `--migrate-game-paths` (default off); fresh repos are already renamed by
  `extract-repos.sh --path-rename`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Generator write gating.** `scaffoldGameRepo`/the CLI accept
   `--only <file,...>` (restrict the run to the named generated files; no other
   file, symlink or rewrite is performed), `--force` (allow overwriting a file
   whose content differs from the template) and `--dry-run` (report every file
   as `create | update | unchanged | skip-local`, writing nothing). Default
   behaviour for extracted repos is unchanged: a full scaffold still writes all
   generated files.
2. **Write reporting.** Every run (dry or real) prints a machine-readable
   summary of the classification per file, so a consumer can see what a run
   would touch before trusting it.
3. **Path rewrite is opt-in.** `example-games/<game>/` → `src/` and the
   accompanying quoted-path/alias rewrites run only with
   `--migrate-game-paths`; without it, no file under `tests/` or `src/` is
   modified. `--migrate-game-paths` also reports the files it rewrites.
4. **Engine tests (test-first).** `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`
   gains tests written **before** the implementation for: `--only` restricting
   writes, `--dry-run` writing nothing while classifying correct, `--force`
   required to replace a diverged file, default-on-path-rewrite removed
   (no-op without the flag) and preserved with the flag. The full engine suite
   passes.
5. **Main-street consumer wiring.** In the `tce-main-street` checkout:
   `package.json`'s `scaffold` script passes `--only main.ts` (plus the flag
   name chosen in AC1); `tests/tooling/scaffold-non-destructive.test.ts` copies
   this repo's `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `index.html`,
   `env.d.ts`, `main.ts` and representative `tests/` files into a temporary
   directory, runs the scaffold against it and fails if any protected wiring
   file changes (while asserting `main.ts` is regenerated);
   `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` replaces the interim "classify-and-revert"
   rule with the new default and opt-in. All related documentation is updated
   (code comments in the generator explain why the overwrite is gated; any
   README or docs-site text describing the scaffold command is corrected).
6. **Stability and validation.** `npm run scaffold` in `tce-main-street` twice in
   a row leaves `git status --porcelain` empty except for opted-in paths; the
   engine pin bump (gitlink + `configs/engine-pin.json` together) is a
   deliberate commit in `tce-main-street`; `npm run build` and the changed-scope
   gate pass there; the full project test suite passes.

## Scope and delivery (two repos)

1. **Engine repo (`Tableau-Card-Engine`, `dev`)** — generator change +
   engine-side tests (AC1–AC4). This is the item's primary worktree.
2. **Consumer repo (`tce-main-street`, `dev`)** — script wiring, regression
   test, docs, engine pin bump (AC5–AC6).

If worktree isolation prevents editing `tce-main-street` from this item's
worktree, create an `MS` follow-up item during planning that carries AC5–AC6
verbatim and link it here; AC5–AC6 must never be dropped.

## Constraints

- **Do not change the default for extracted repos.** The eight sibling repos
  (`tce-golf` etc.) keep the plain `scaffold` invocation and must still receive
  template updates from a full run.
- **Never run the destructive path** against a live checkout while developing;
  experiment in a temp directory or the worktree.
- **Engine pin discipline:** the pin (`configs/engine-pin.json`) and the `core`
  gitlink travel together in one deliberate commit; never a build side effect.
- Repository boundaries: only the generator, its tests, the consumer
  `package.json`/docs/tests and the engine pin are in scope.

## Existing state

- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`: `writeFile()` writes unconditionally
  (no content comparison, no dry-run, no allow-list); `parseArgs` supports only
  `--game`, `--game-repo-root`, `--core-root`, `--core-rel`, `--version`,
  `--all`, `--repos-dir`, `--layout`.
- `rewriteGameTreePaths()` walks all of `tests/**` and `src/**` and applies four
  textual rewrites to every `.ts/.tsx/.mjs/.cjs/.js` file whether or not it
  references the game tree.
- `index.html` is copied verbatim from `core/index.html`; `renderPackageJson`
  inherits the core's scripts and dependencies — both clobber local wiring in a
  live checkout.
- One observed run on a clean `dev` tree rewrote 11 files besides `main.ts`,
  including the drift guard's own `STALE_PREFIX`, a run-tests import (`→
  @core-scripts/run-tests`) and 250 lines of documented LOCAL SURGICAL
  ADDITIONS in `vite.config.ts`. Full table on `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB`.

## Key Files

- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — write gating (`--only`, `--force`,
  `--dry-run`), classification reporting, `--migrate-game-paths` gating in
  `scaffoldGameRepo` + `parseArgs`, rationale comments.
- `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — engine-side tests (AC4).
- `tce-main-street/package.json` — scope the `scaffold` script.
- `tce-main-street/tests/tooling/scaffold-non-destructive.test.ts` — new
  regression guard (temp-copy harness); follow the style of
  `tests/tooling/phaser-single-copy.test.ts`.
- `tce-main-street/docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — document default + opt-in.
- `tce-main-street/configs/engine-pin.json` — pin bump.
- `tce-main-street/main.ts`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `index.html` —
  protected inputs for the regression harness (not to be edited).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `main.ts` is the only file main-street currently wants
  regenerated (per `MS-0MVU03TR0006KZDH`).
- **Risk:** a cross-repo delivery from one worktree may violate worktree
  isolation — mitigated by the explicit split-and-link rule above.
- **Risk:** `--only` interacting with symlink/asset linking could leave a repo
  half-scaffolded — mitigate by making `--only` skip links entirely and
  reporting that it did.
- **Risk:** temp-copy harness drift — mitigate by copying real repo files rather
  than inlining fixtures.
- **Scope-creep risk:** generator script hygiene (broken `scaffold:game` keys)
  is tracked separately in `MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0`; link, do not absorb.

## Related work

- `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB` — origin item (intake brief, producer decisions,
  observed damage table). Closed on creation of this item.
- `MS-0MVU03TR0006KZDH` / `MS-0MVTMJ2GA008GRZ7` — the re-scaffold that exposed
  the hazard.
- `MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0` and children — generator-emitted script hygiene
  (separate scope).
- `MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0` — template improvement that relies on re-scaffold
  remaining usable.
- `CG-0MVPWPWLA008FTDJ`, `CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA` — precedent template fixes that
  re-scaffold propagates.

## Plan (2026-10-31)

**Decomposition — five child items, test-first inside each slice.** Test-first is satisfied *within* each child (failing tests authored first, then the implementation, then a green build → test → commit cycle); no standalone RED child exists because this repo gates every commit on a green suite, so a tests-only child could not be committed. The children cut vertically through the layers they touch: generator code, generator tests, CLI `--help`, and the rationale/doc prose that belongs to the slice. Consumer prose lives in the engine docs child; the consumer repo work is the MS follow-up.

| # | Child | Slice | Parent ACs |
|---|-------|-------|------------|
| 1 | `CG-0MVWGJNQM0061W6I` Scaffold write classification, dry-run and report | classification pipeline, `--dry-run`, `--json` report, typed `ScaffoldResult.files` | AC1 (`--dry-run`), AC2, AC4 |
| 2 | `CG-0MVWGJPPA000GBE7` Only allow-list, force and skip-local gating | `--only`, `--force`, `skip-local`, side-effect suppression, fail-fast name validation | AC1, AC4 |
| 3 | `CG-0MVWGJRIO0094Y4Z` Gate path rewrite behind migrate-game-paths | `--migrate-game-paths` opt-in, dry-run preview, mutual exclusion with `--only` | AC3, AC4 |
| 4 | `CG-0MVWGJTDL00576GQ` Document scaffold write gating in engine docs | `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, generator header cross-reference | AC5 (docs clause) |
| 5 | `CG-0MVWGJUU3003J7HA` Main-street wiring, guard, docs and pin bump | cross-repo delivery, tracked as `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0` (AC5 + AC6 verbatim) | AC5, AC6 |

**Dependency order:** 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 (`wl dep add` edges wired). Child 5 is a tracking/verification child: the code, test, doc and pin-bump work is executed in `tce-main-street` under `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0`, because this item's worktree (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-…`) cannot write outside the core checkout — the parent's own scope note requires exactly this split, and AC5–AC6 must not be dropped.

**Recorded design decision (AC1's `--force` interaction).** AC1 lists `--force` and the `skip-local` classification, while the Constraints require a plain full run to keep propagating template updates to the eight sibling repos. The only reading in which both hold — and in which `--force` is not dead code — is:

- **No `--only`** → today's behaviour: every diverged generated file is rewritten (`update`). Implemented as `effectiveForce = force || only === undefined`.
- **With `--only`** → only the named files are candidates; a named file that exists and differs is `skip-local` (untouched) unless `--force` is passed, and every unselected file is `skip-local`. Selection mode suppresses the `core` symlink, shared-asset links, root app-icon links and the game-tree path rewrite entirely.
- `--only` + `--migrate-game-paths` is rejected as a conflict (selection promises "no rewrite").

Consequence: the `tce-main-street` scaffold script becomes `--only main.ts --force` (AC5's "plus the flag name chosen in AC1"). This interpretation is implemented by children 2–3 and consumed by `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0`; it is recorded here so the audit can check intent rather than re-derive it.

**Other recorded assumptions**

- `main.ts` is the only file `tce-main-street` wants regenerated (per `MS-0MVU03TR0006KZDH`); `configs/game.json` may be opted in later by the same mechanism.
- `--json` is the machine-readable report surface (one document per run: an object for `--game`, an array for `--all`); the classification vocabulary stays exactly `create | update | unchanged | skip-local`.
- The generator's script-hygiene defects (`scaffold:game` keys) stay with `MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0` — linked, not absorbed.

**Duplicate check:** `wl search scaffold` / `wl search "scaffold generator write gating"` against the core store returned no non-terminal overlapping item; the closest completed items (`CG-0MVSIB5LH0069LB3`, `CG-0MVPWPWLA008FTDJ`, `CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA`) are template fixes this plan's full-run back-compatibility must keep propagating.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The producer answered the design questions on `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB` (2026-10-31) before this item was created; that record is the authoritative source and is not re-asked here.

- Q1: "Should the generator change its default, or expose explicit selection while keeping today's default?" Answer (producer): "**B — explicit selection, not a changed default.** Keep today's behaviour for fresh/extracted game repos; add `--only <file,...>`, `--force` and `--dry-run`; the main-street `scaffold` script opts in to `main.ts` only." Final: B.
- Q2: "Which repo owns the generator change, and does it also own the consumer wiring?" Answer (producer): "**A — this item owns the generator change**, test-first in the engine repo, followed by an engine pin bump in `tce-main-street`." Final: A.
- Q3: "Should `rewriteGameTreePaths` stay on by default?" Answer (producer): "**A — `rewriteGameTreePaths` becomes opt-in** via `--migrate-game-paths` (default off); fresh repos are already renamed by `extract-repos.sh --path-rename`." Final: A.
- Q (planning, resolved without escalation): "Does a selected file that diverges from the template get written unconditionally, or only with `--force`?" Answer (plan, from AC1 + the extracted-repo constraint): only with `--force`; a full run keeps today's unconditional rewrite. Recorded as the "Recorded design decision" above. Evidence: AC1 (`--force` "allow overwriting a file whose content differs from the template"), Constraints ("the eight sibling repos … must still receive template updates from a full run").
- Q (planning, resolved without escalation): "Can `tce-main-street` be edited from this item's worktree?" Answer (plan, from the parent's scope note + worktree isolation): no — create the `MS` follow-up `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0` carrying AC5–AC6 verbatim. Final: MS follow-up created.
- Q (planning, resolved without escalation): "Which consumer docs still describe the scaffold command?" Answer (plan, repo inspection): `tce-main-street/docs/dev/build-and-release.md` (re-scaffold references) and `tce-main-street/docs/dev/testing.md` (three passages claiming `npm run scaffold` regenerates the `resolve.dedupe` and transcript-persist wiring). The MS follow-up corrects both; the engine docs child covers `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `README.md`.

**OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking, for the audit review):** none — the flagged interpretation above is an implementation detail inside the producer's fixed design space, documented rather than escalated.
data.title: Scaffold generator: opt-in write gating and an explicit game-path migration flag

# Main-street consumer wiring, guard, docs and pin bump

**Parent:** `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` — the cross-repo delivery of AC5 and AC6.

**Delivery vehicle:** `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0` — _Make npm run scaffold non-destructive: wiring, guard, docs and pin bump_ (created in the `tce-main-street` Worklog store at plan time, carrying AC5 and AC6 verbatim).

## Why this child exists

Worktree isolation forbids this item's worktree from editing the sibling `tce-main-street` checkout (a `CG` implementation runs inside `.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-<id>-<slug>`, and every write must resolve inside it). The parent's scope note therefore requires an `MS` follow-up item carrying AC5–AC6 verbatim, linked here, so the consumer work is tracked in the store that owns it and **cannot be dropped**.

This child is therefore a **tracking and verification** item, not a second implementation:

- The code, test, doc and pin-bump work happens under `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0`.
- This child is closed when `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0` is verified complete (stage `in_review`/`completed`) and its evidence is summarised on this item and on the parent.

## Acceptance Criteria

Carried over verbatim from `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` (AC5, AC6):

- **Main-street consumer wiring.** In the `tce-main-street` checkout: `package.json`'s `scaffold` script passes `--only main.ts` (plus the flag name chosen in AC1); `tests/tooling/scaffold-non-destructive.test.ts` copies this repo's `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `index.html`, `env.d.ts`, `main.ts` and representative `tests/` files into a temporary directory, runs the scaffold against it and fails if any protected wiring file changes (while asserting `main.ts` is regenerated); `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` replaces the interim "classify-and-revert" rule with the new default and opt-in. All related documentation is updated (code comments in the generator explain why the overwrite is gated; any README or docs-site text describing the scaffold command is corrected).
- **Stability and validation.** `npm run scaffold` in `tce-main-street` twice in a row leaves `git status --porcelain` empty except for opted-in paths; the engine pin bump (gitlink + `configs/engine-pin.json` together) is a deliberate commit in `tce-main-street`; `npm run build` and the changed-scope gate pass there; the full project test suite passes.

Additional tracking criteria for this child:

- `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0` exists in the `tce-main-street` store, carries AC5–AC6 verbatim, and references this parent.
- The consumer work is delivered as committed, pushed `dev`-branch work in `tce-main-street` (never `main`), with the commit hash and the engine pin SHA recorded on both `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0` and this item.
- The engine pin bump references an engine `dev` commit that contains the gating work (gitlink and `configs/engine-pin.json` in one deliberate commit).
- Evidence for both verbatim ACs (scoped `scaffold` script, temp-copy regression guard result, corrected docs, double-run `git status --porcelain` output, build + changed-scope gate + full suite results) is quoted or linked in a comment on this item.

## Minimal Implementation

- Verify, on this item, that `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0` has reached a terminal state with all its ACs evidenced.
- Cross-check the two verbatim ACs against the MS item's evidence line by line (script arguments, guard test name and result, docs files touched, pin SHA equality between `configs/engine-pin.json` and the `core` gitlink, double-run cleanliness, gate results).
- Record the summary comment (with the MS commit hash, engine pin SHA, and the verified evidence) on this item, then link it from the parent's completion comment.

**Key Files:**

- `tce-main-street/package.json` — scoped `scaffold` script (`--only main.ts --force`).
- `tce-main-street/tests/tooling/scaffold-non-destructive.test.ts` — temp-copy regression guard.
- `tce-main-street/docs/dev/build-and-release.md`, `tce-main-street/docs/dev/testing.md` — documented default + opt-in (and corrected scaffold-regenerates-wiring claims).
- `tce-main-street/configs/engine-pin.json` and the `core` gitlink — pin bump travelling together.

## Dependencies

- `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` child: _Document scaffold write gating in the engine docs_ (and transitively the three generator slices) — the pinned engine commit must already contain `--only`, `--force`, `--dry-run`, `--json` and `--migrate-game-paths`.

## Deliverables

A verified, committed, `dev`-only delivery in `tce-main-street`: non-destructive `npm run scaffold`, the temp-copy regression guard, corrected docs, and a deliberate engine pin bump — with the evidence quoted on this item and on the parent.

# Remove the legacy two-way choice code from storylines

## Problem statement

The core story-line system still carries the original **two-way choice** data
model (`hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`) as a transitional
fallback alongside the generalised `options` model, plus the two-way
`ChoiceClarityLabels` presentation API (`StorylineUiAdapter.choiceClarityLabels`
/ `defaultChoiceClarityLabels`). Two compilation paths, two authoring/editor
field sets, two validation vocabularies and a two-button label API must be
maintained, and editors can silently no-op when they edit the legacy links of
an `options`-authored card. The generalised model (`options` encoding +
programmatic registry) now covers every shipped case, so the legacy model and
its clarity-label API should be deleted end-to-end.

The work item seed explicitly waives backward compatibility and directs that
the `../tce-main-street` story-lines be inspected; if they use the legacy
structure, a **critical** work item must be created in that project to update
them. The producer has additionally confirmed that `ChoiceClarityLabels` is
in scope for retirement.

## Users

- **Engine maintainer** — "As the maintainer of `src/story-line/`, I want one
  option model and one compilation path so I no longer carry dead transitional
  code and conditional `hasChoices` branches."
- **Game developer (Main Street / future games)** — "As a game developer, I
  want a single documented way to author choices (`options` encoding or the
  registry) so my content, adapter, CLI and editor all agree."
- **Content designer** — "As a content designer, I want the editor and
  `storylines:author` CLI to expose only supported fields, so an edit cannot
  silently do nothing because it wrote a legacy link column."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Runtime model and clarity-label API removed.** `StorylineCard.hasChoices`,
   `acceptNextCardId` and `rejectNextCardId` are gone from `src/story-line/types.ts`;
   `compileStorylineFromEvent` compiles only from registered options or a
   non-empty CSV `options` encoding (no Accept/Reject fallback), and
   `eventHasStoryline` no longer consults `hasChoices`. `ChoiceClarityLabels`,
   `StorylineUiAdapter.choiceClarityLabels` and `defaultChoiceClarityLabels` are
   removed from the public API (and their `index.ts` exports). A bare
   `storylineId` still does **not** make a card a choice. All shipped content
   compiles to exactly the same option lists as before.
2. **Content/authoring/editor toolchain removed.** The content model
   (`ContentCard`, `ContentFieldMapping`, `mappedFieldColumns`), CSV
   projection (`cardsFromCsv`), content compilation (`compileContentOptions`,
   `contentCardHasChoice`), validator (`orphan-link` / `dangling-link` legacy
   rules), `mutate` specs, editor view-model/field-descriptors/`linkKind`
   edits, `storyline-author` CLI flags, and the visual editor forms no longer
   model, read, write, validate or expose the three legacy fields. A derived
   *choice-node* flag (e.g. the manifest's `hasChoices`) may remain **only** if
   it is computed purely from compiled options.
3. **Content artefacts, fixtures and schema aligned.** The Gym demo content
   (`example-games/gym/content/storylines.csv`) drops the three legacy columns
   and `GYM_CONTENT_ADAPTER` stops mapping them; the committed Gym manifest /
   Mermaid artefacts regenerate with no drift (`npm run storylines:graph --
   --check`); card-pack fixtures, reference CSVs and
   `schemas/story-line-manifest.schema.json` are updated consistently.
4. **Main Street investigated and follow-up filed.** `../tce-main-street` is
   inspected. Because its CSV header, `MAIN_STREET_CONTENT_ADAPTER`,
   `EventCard` type, transcript schema, `MainStreetStorylineJournal`
   (`ChoiceClarityLabels` re-export + `choiceClarityLabels`) and storyline
   helpers still declare the legacy columns/fields/API, a **critical** work
   item is created in the `tce-main-street` Worklog to remove them and migrate
   its loader/resolution/presentation to the `options`-only model (push to
   `dev` only).
5. **Docs and tests.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, `docs/core-engine/story-line.md`,
   `docs/dev/storyline-editor.md` and `docs/dev/card-packs-runbook.md`, and no
   reference to the three legacy fields remains in `src/`, `tools/`, `scripts/`,
   `schemas/` or `example-games/`. Unit and browser tests are updated (legacy
   fixtures replaced with `options` equivalents), the changed-scope test gate
   passes, and the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Backward compatibility is explicitly **not** required (seed).
- Preserve every generalised-model behaviour: arbitrary labels, ordered
  candidate successor sets, terminal options, `effectPolicy: 'apply'` for CSV
  options, registry precedence, conditional/cost draw-time filtering, and
  exactly one seeded `rng()` draw per random successor selection.
- `StorylineOption.successorId` is **not** part of the legacy two-way removal:
  it remains the registry seam field and the lowest-precedence single successor.
- `ChoiceClarityLabels` **is** retired (producer instruction). The
  `accept`/`reject` narrative wording in `defaultStoryUpdateLine` remains: it is
  driven by the option label, not by the retired label API, and Main Street's
  dialogs still present Accept/Reject option labels.
- Core must stay Phaser-free and game-free; the content toolchain must load
  under `tsx` and keep byte-identical CSV round-trips.
- Multi-repo: core changes land in this repo; Main Street changes are tracked
  in its own Worklog store and pushed to `dev` only (never `main`).
- No `wl list` without a search term; use the standard `build → test → commit`
  order during implementation.

## Existing state

- The generalised option model was introduced by MS-0MV8KQJR30007JL5 and
  generalised into core by CG-0MVHZ2KE40011Z0S; the legacy fields were kept
  transitionally.
- Main Street `src/card-data.csv`: **no** row populates the three legacy
  columns (all blank / `false`); 7 rows use the `options` encoding.
- Gym `example-games/gym/content/storylines.csv`: the three legacy columns are
  present in the header but every row has them blank / `false`; 3 rows use
  `options`.
- The committed Gym manifest and schema still carry a (derived) `hasChoices`
  node flag.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` still documents the legacy compilation
  precedence, the "game without a legacy two-way choice model" adapter
  guidance, and the `choiceClarityLabels` UI-adapter method.
- `StorylineUiAdapter` still requires `choiceClarityLabels`, implemented by
  `defaultChoiceClarityLabels`; Main Street re-exports the type and wraps the
  method in `MainStreetStorylineJournal`.

## Desired change

Delete the legacy two-way choice model and the `ChoiceClarityLabels` API
end-to-end, leaving a single `options`/registry-driven choice model, and align

- `src/story-line/content/manifest.ts` — derive choice-ness from compiled

- `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` — drop legacy columns/mappings/defaults

- CG-0MVHZ2RBJ004O0VD — Storyline management UI.

  Main Street storylines).
- CG-0MVKNC9MY006ULES — Gym storyline demo: extract pure logic and unit-test it.
- MS-0MV8KQJR30007JL5 — CSV option encoding and compilation (Main Street;
  introduced `options`, intended to retire the three legacy columns).
- MS-0MVCRQ475009CDZI — Extract the storyline features (Main Street).
- MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144 — Allow multiple possible outcomes from storyline nodes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Decision — `ChoiceClarityLabels` retired.** The producer confirmed the
  accept/reject clarity-label API is in scope; it is removed from `types.ts`,
  `ui-adapter.ts` and `index.ts`. The `accept`/`reject` narrative wording in
  `defaultStoryUpdateLine` is retained (label-driven, separate from the retired
  API) unless the producer asks for that too.
- **Assumption — `successorId` retained.** It is the registry seam and the
  lowest-precedence single successor, not part of the two-way removal.
- **Assumption — derived choice flag retained.** The manifest's node choice
  flag (currently `hasChoices`) may stay if computed purely from compiled
  options; renaming is optional polish, not required.
- **Risk — silent behaviour drift.** Removing the fallback could change
  compilation for a content row that relied on `hasChoices` with no `options`.

  legacy columns (verified), so expected drift is zero for shipped content.

  submodule; deleting the exported fields and the `ChoiceClarityLabels` API
  breaks its build until its own item lands. Mitigation: file the critical Main
  Street item as part of this work and land/pin the submodule bump together.

  committed Gym artefacts in the same commit.
- **Scope-creep guard.** Renaming the derived manifest node flag is recorded
  as optional polish, not folded into this item unless the producer says
  otherwise. Retiring the `defaultStoryUpdateLine` accept/reject narrative
  wording is likewise a separate decision if wanted.

  `../tce-main-street/src/MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts`).
- Q: "Do the Main Street story-lines use the legacy structure?" — Answer

  `false` in `src/card-data.csv`, and 7 rows use the `options` encoding.

  `MainStreetStorylineContentAdapter.ts`, `MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`,
  `MainStreetTranscript.ts`, `MainStreetStoryline.ts`,
  `MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts`.
- Q: "Is backward compatibility required?" — Answer (seed): **No**.

# Options-parity golden snapshot for shipped story-line content

## Summary

Pin the behaviour this refactor must not change, before any deletion happens.
Record the compiled option list of every shipped story-line card in a committed
golden fixture and add a unit test that recompiles the content and compares. The
test is green today and must stay green after every removal phase, so any
compilation drift surfaces immediately instead of at the end of the epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A committed fixture `tests/fixtures/story-line/options-parity.json` records, per shipped card id: card name, storyline id, and the ordered compiled options (label, ordered successor ids, `effectPolicy`).
- The fixture covers the Gym content (`example-games/gym/content/storylines.csv` compiled with `GYM_CONTENT_ADAPTER`) and the Main Street reference-pack copy (`tests/fixtures/reference-packs/main-street/main-street/main-street-foundations/cards.csv` compiled with a minimal options-only adapter declared in the test).
- A unit test recompiles both files through the public content API (`cardsFromCsv` then `compileContentOptions`) and deep-equals the fixture, so drift fails with a readable diff.
- Explicit assertions (on top of the deep-equal) cover at least one multi-option card, one terminal option (`successorIds: []`) and one plain incident with an empty option list, so the intent of the snapshot is legible without reading the fixture.
- The test passes against the current pre-refactor code: the baseline is captured from real behaviour, not hand-written.
- The test asserts shipped-content behaviour (CSV in, compiled options out); it is not a source-code grep over `src/`.

## Key Files

- `tests/story-line/options-parity.test.ts` — new golden-parity test (unit profile).
- `tests/fixtures/story-line/options-parity.json` — new committed golden fixture.
- `example-games/gym/content/storylines.csv` — the shipped Gym content the snapshot pins.
- `tests/fixtures/reference-packs/main-street/main-street/main-street-foundations/cards.csv` — the shipped Main Street reference copy the snapshot pins.
- `src/story-line/content/csv.ts` — the projection/compilation entry points the test drives.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the test so it builds the snapshot from the shipped CSVs and prints the computed JSON when it mismatches.
2. Run it once, review the captured snapshot for plausibility (labels and orders must match the `options` encodings in both CSVs), and commit it as the golden.
3. Add the three representative assertions alongside the deep-equal.

## Deliverables

- Golden fixture plus parity test running in the unit profile.
- A doc comment in the test recording what it pins, which adapters it uses, and when the baseline was captured.

## Dependencies

None — safe to land first.

## Provenance

Child of CG-0MVZBUWPH003PWUI. Enforces parent AC1 ("All shipped content
compiles to exactly the same option lists as before") and de-risks AC3/AC5.

# Retire legacy choice fields and the clarity-label API from the runtime model

## Summary

Delete the transitional two-way choice model from the runtime: the
`StorylineCard` fields `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId` and `rejectNextCardId`,
the Accept/Reject compilation branch, the `hasChoices` clause in
`eventHasStoryline`, and the whole `ChoiceClarityLabels` presentation API.
Compilation then reads only registered options or a non-empty CSV `options`
encoding, and the Gym demo renders its two-button labels straight from the
compiled option labels.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `StorylineCard` has no `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId` or `rejectNextCardId`, and no module under `src/story-line/` reads them.
- `compileStorylineFromEvent` compiles only from registered programmatic options or a non-empty CSV `options` encoding; a card with a bare `storylineId` and no options still yields an empty option list and `eventHasStoryline` returns `false` for it (a bare `storylineId` never makes a card a choice).
- `ChoiceClarityLabels`, `StorylineUiAdapter.choiceClarityLabels` and `defaultChoiceClarityLabels` are removed from `src/story-line/types.ts`, `src/story-line/ui-adapter.ts` and the `src/story-line/index.ts` barrel; `createDefaultStorylineUiAdapter` no longer supplies the method.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymStorylineScene.ts` derives its accept/reject button labels from the compiled option labels instead of calling `system.ui.choiceClarityLabels(...)`, and still presents two buttons for the Gym's two-option cards.
- Preservation is asserted by passing unit tests for every generalised behaviour: arbitrary labels, ordered candidate successor sets, terminal options, `effectPolicy: 'apply'` for CSV options, registry precedence over CSV, draw-time conditional/cost filtering, exactly one seeded `rng()` draw per random successor selection, and `StorylineOption.successorId` remaining the lowest-precedence single successor.
- `defaultStoryUpdateLine`'s accept/reject narrative wording is unchanged (it is label-driven, not part of the retired API) and its existing tests still pass.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` no longer documents the legacy compilation precedence, the "game without a legacy two-way choice model" adapter guidance, or the `choiceClarityLabels` UI-adapter method.
- Changed-scope unit tests pass (`/skill:test --type unit`) and `npm run build` succeeds.
- **Satisfies parent AC1 of CG-0MVZBUWPH003PWUI.** **Runtime model and clarity-label API removed.** `StorylineCard.hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId` and `rejectNextCardId` are gone from `src/story-line/types.ts`; `compileStorylineFromEvent` compiles only from registered options or a non-empty CSV `options` encoding (no Accept/Reject fallback), and `eventHasStoryline` no longer consults `hasChoices`. `ChoiceClarityLabels`, `StorylineUiAdapter.choiceClarityLabels` and `defaultChoiceClarityLabels` are removed from the public API (and their `index.ts` exports). A bare `storylineId` still does **not** make a card a choice. All shipped content compiles to exactly the same option lists as before.

## Key Files

- `src/story-line/types.ts` — drop the three card fields, the `ChoiceClarityLabels` interface and the UI-adapter method.
- `src/story-line/compile.ts` — delete the legacy Accept/Reject branch and the `hasChoices` clause of `eventHasStoryline`.
- `src/story-line/ui-adapter.ts` — delete `defaultChoiceClarityLabels` and its `createDefaultStorylineUiAdapter` entry.
- `src/story-line/index.ts` — drop the retired type and helper exports.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymStorylineScene.ts` — render choice labels from compiled options.
- `tests/story-line/compile.test.ts` — rewrite legacy-compilation cases as options-only cases.
- `tests/story-line/ui-adapter.test.ts` — drop the `choiceClarityLabels` suite.
- `tests/story-line/resolve.test.ts` — drop legacy-resolution fixtures.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — compilation-precedence and UI-adapter sections.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Remove the legacy types and compilation branch; replace the Accept/Reject test cases with `options`-encoded equivalents.
2. Delete the clarity-label API and update the Gym scene to use `option.label` for the two buttons.
3. Reword the affected `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` sections to the single-model story.

Note: the content toolchain (`src/story-line/content/`, `src/story-line/editor/`)
still carries its own `ContentCard` legacy fields at this point, so the tree
stays green; those are removed by the next child.

## Deliverables

- Runtime model and clarity-label API removed, with tests rewritten to the options model.
- In-phase docs update for the runtime/adapter sections.
- Clean `npm run build`.

## Dependencies

- `CG-0MVZBUWPH003PWUI` child "Options-parity golden snapshot for shipped story-line content" (test-first ordering; the snapshot guards this phase).

## Provenance

Child of CG-0MVZBUWPH003PWUI, satisfying parent AC1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `ManifestNode.hasChoices` becomes `ManifestNode.isChoice`, documented as derived from compiled options only; `renderMermaid` and every other manifest consumer use the new name.
- `schemas/story-line-manifest.schema.json` renames the required property, and `tests/story-line/editor/manifest-schema.test.ts` validates the regenerated Gym manifest against the schema.

- A reference sweep over `src/`, `tools/`, `scripts/`, `schemas/`, `example-games/` and `tests/` finds zero occurrences of `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId` and `ChoiceClarityLabels`.
- Changed-scope unit and browser tests pass (editor viewer + round-trip included) and `npm run build` succeeds.

- `src/story-line/editor/view-model.ts` — expose `isChoice`.
